alex: Morning — quick async standup from the priming/latency experiments I ran on canary nodes.
alex: TL;DR: cold-start p95 ~230ms, after priming p95 ~62ms. KV hit-rate jumped 18% -> 76% with prefetch enabled.
alex: Command I used to run the microbench (canary):
```bash
./bench_runner --model=redwood-v-lite --seq=512 --concurrency=8 --prefetch=true --prefetch-ttl=45
```
maria: Nice. Which prefetch TTL did you set for that run? and did you pre-warm the slots or rely on passive priming?
alex: ttl=45s, passive priming only (no manual slot pin). I also tested ttl=120s — hit-rate slightly higher but CPU went up ~6%.
chris: Thanks for the numbers. I pushed batching heuristic change in PR #8214 to avoid growing microbatches for <8ms tails. Can someone review? It's small but touches slotting logic.
sasha: Reviewing traces now — the prefetch stage added a spike in kernel user CPU for the first 3s of a slot lifecycle. Looks like we're firing 6 prefetch requests/concurrency instead of 2.
sasha: Suggestion: cap prefetch concurrency with a new flag `--prefetch-concurrency=2` and tune from there.
jordan: I can take PR #8214 review in the afternoon and run the bench with prefetch-concurrency=2. Will post results here.
maria: Also, are we comfortable setting default prefetch-ttl to 45s for Dedicated? Seems like a reasonable tradeoff, but ops might want lower for high churn workloads.
alex: Blockers: need one more reviewer on #8214 and a decision on default TTL for Dedicated. If we set ttl too low we lose hit-rate; too high and we blow CPU in spikes.
alex: Today: run cross-shard priming bench, test prefetch-concurrency=2 and 4, and update perf dashboard with broken-out CPU by prefetch vs kernel.
deploy-bot: canary: redwood-runtime v2.3.7 deployed to canary cluster (c-17). monitoring alerts suppressed for 10m.
chris: re: alerts suppression — fyi we'll keep an eye on eviction rates. If eviction > 12% during priming, roll back prefetch defaults.
jordan: quick note — I'll also attach the raw bench logs after my runs so we have numbers to compare (tokens/sec, cold p95, warmed p95).
alex: great, thanks. ping @jordan @chris when you have bench logs. :thumbsup:
